items.text: Drink sufficient water regularly during hot weather, even when you do not feel thirsty. People on fluid-restricted diets or with conditions affecting fluid intake should consult their doctor before increasing fluids.
Wear lightweight, light-coloured, loose cotton clothing. When outdoors, protect your head with a hat, cloth or umbrella.
Take extra care of older adults, children and people who are ill, as they are more vulnerable to excessive heat.
Outdoor workplaces should provide cool drinking water, shaded resting areas and first-aid supplies. Schedule strenuous work during cooler hours and provide frequent rest breaks.

Common signs of heat stress include dizziness, headache, weakness, excessive sweating, rapid heartbeat, nausea and muscle cramps. Move to a cooler or shaded place, stop strenuous activity and seek medical advice if symptoms persist or worsen.

If someone faints or shows signs of confusion, seizures or suspected heat stroke, seek emergency medical help immediately. Move the person to a cooler place and begin cooling them while waiting for medical assistance. Do not delay emergency care.
Rainwater harvesting collects and stores rainwater or helps recharge groundwater. Rooftop rainwater harvesting can use suitable recharge pits, trenches or wells.
Rainwater harvesting systems require appropriate design and maintenance. Keep collection areas clean and filter rainwater before directing it into a recharge well.
